comparisons.peer_topic: AI Software Ecosystem and Silo AI Acquisition
comparisons.peer_summary: To support its AI strategy, AMD consolidated AI teams to develop a comprehensive software ecosystem, improved AMD ROCm software performance, and acquired Silo AI Oy to accelerate AI model development and deployment on AMD hardware, leveraging Silo's software stack for training large language models.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies emphasize the importance of software ecosystems and strategic acquisitions to enhance their core hardware capabilities in the AI era. Intel highlights its 'robust design ecosystem with key industry partners' and 'systems of chips capabilities' as advantages for co-optimized AI solutions. AMD similarly focuses on executing its AI strategy through a 'comprehensive software ecosystem' and strategic acquisitions like Silo AI to accelerate the 'development and deployment of AI models on AMD hardware,' mirroring Intel's focus on ecosystem and integration for AI performance.

sentences.text: Our foundry offerings benefit from several key advantages: our robust design ecosystem with key industry partners; our systems of chips capabilities; and our secure, resilient, and sustainable supply chain.
Our foundry is built on the foundation of our silicon process and advanced packaging technology offerings and enables co-optimized solutions for the AI era.
To execute our AI strategy, we brought together multiple AI teams across AMD to drive development of a comprehensive software ecosystem spanning our full product portfolio.
The acquisition of Silo AI enables customers to accelerate development and deployment of AI models on AMD hardware.

comparisons.peer_topic: Strategic Focus on Leadership and Acquisitions
comparisons.peer_summary: The company's strategy focuses on technology leadership and category-leading solutions, achieved through strategic acquisitions and extensive internal research and development to drive diversified and sustainable results.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom (Avago) describe their competitive positioning through technology leadership achieved via internal R&D and strategic acquisitions. Intel cites its 'silicon process and advanced packaging technology offerings' as the foundation for its foundry advantages, while Broadcom states its strategy is to achieve 'technology leadership and category-leading semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions' through 'strategic acquisitions of businesses and technologies, as well as extensive internal research and development.' Both frame their market position around combining technological depth with strategic M&A or ecosystem building.

sentences.text: Our foundry is built on the foundation of our silicon process and advanced packaging technology offerings and enables co-optimized solutions for the AI era.

Our strategy is focused on technology leadership and category-leading semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions delivering a comprehensive suite of innovative infrastructure technology products to the world's leading business and government customers.

We seek to achieve this through strategic acquisitions of businesses and technologies, as well as extensive internal research and development, to ensure our products retain their technology market leadership.

comparisons.peer_topic: CHIPS Act-funded U.S. fab expansion plans and timeline
comparisons.peer_summary: Plans to invest in two U.S. fab facilities were announced following the CHIPS Act: construction began in Boise, Idaho in October 2023 with output projected in 2027, and a second facility in Clay, New York is expected to begin site preparation in 2025 with production ramping in the latter half of the decade, intended to meet future wafer capacity demand.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose strategic expansions of their U.S. manufacturing capabilities to address future capacity needs, though the contexts differ: Intel's Foundry division highlights its existing robust supply chain and ecosystem advantages, while Micron details specific capital investment plans for new fab facilities supported by government incentives. Intel emphasizes its 'secure, resilient, and sustainable supply chain' as a key advantage, whereas Micron explicitly links its new facility plans to the 'U.S. CHIPS and Science Act' and projected demand, stating that new fabs are 'key to meeting our requirements for additional wafer capacity.'

sentences.text: Our foundry offerings benefit from several key advantages: our robust design ecosystem with key industry partners; our systems of chips capabilities; and our secure, resilient, and sustainable supply chain.

Following the enactment of the U.S. CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 ("CHIPS Act"), we announced plans to invest in two leading-edge memory manufacturing fab facilities in the United States, based on CHIPS Act support through grants and investment tax credits.

We expect these new fabs to be key to meeting our requirements for additional wafer capacity starting in the second half of the decade and beyond, in line with industry demand trends and to maintain an objective of stable bit share.
